vo.en: Nobody is actually looking at you.

visual.description: A busy city sidewalk with many pedestrians walking in different directions, blurred slightly.

vo.en: Ever felt like a tiny mistake was a neon sign pointing at you? That’s the spotlight effect.

visual.description: A nervous person standing in a public place looking down at their clothes.

vo.en: In a famous study, researchers found people overestimate how much others notice them by fifty percent.

visual.description: A clean motion graphic showing a percentage bar filling up or a simple bar chart.

vo.en: While you’re obsessing over that awkward thing you said, everyone else is busy worrying about themselves.

visual.description: Commuters on a train all looking at their own phones or looking out the window.

vo.en: Think about it. Do you remember the stain on your coworker’s shirt from three days ago? Probably not.

visual.description: A close up of a small coffee stain on a white shirt sleeve.

vo.en: We are the center of our own universe, making us think we’re the center of everyone else’s too.

visual.description: A cinematic shot of a galaxy or rotating stars in the night sky.

vo.en: This realization is the ultimate freedom. You can stop performing and just exist without the constant pressure.

visual.description: A person standing on a hill or balcony taking a deep, relaxed breath.

vo.en: You’re far less judged than you think. Relax. Follow for more psychological insights to calm your mind.

visual.description: Calm ocean waves gently lapping at the shore during a golden sunset.
